title: La visite imprévue de José  (José's Unexpected Visit)

segments.t: Late at night in her apartment, Andrea Martel worries about Colette's sudden silence. Her anxious thoughts are shattered when actor Jose Garcia knocks loudly at her door in high spirits. Let's listen to their chaotic encounter in French first.
Andréa! Ouvre la porte, c'est moi!
José? Qu'est-ce que tu fais là?
Quelle nuit incroyable, Andréa!
Chut! Parle doucement, s'il te plaît.
Mon bébé dort dans la chambre.
Oh pardon, je veux voir ta fille!
Non, reste ici dans le salon.
Tu es magnifique ce soir, Andréa!
Mais tu as bu beaucoup d'alcool!
Oui, j'ai passé la soirée avec Laurence.
Tu dois te reposer pour ton tournage.
Je peux me servir à boire?
Bois seulement de l'eau fraîche maintenant.
D'accord, je vais me calmer un peu.
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Andréa! Ouvre la porte, c'est moi!
'Andrea! Open the door, it is me!' Jose calls out enthusiastically from the hallway. The familiar imperative 'open' commands someone you know well.
José? Qu'est-ce que tu fais là?
'Jose? What are you doing here?' Andrea opens her door in complete bewilderment. The question structure 'what'est-ce que' is the standard way to ask what in French.
Quelle nuit incroyable, Andréa!
'What an incredible night, Andrea!' Jose cannot contain his excitement after an evening out. The exclamative adjective 'incredible' expresses overwhelming surprise.
Chut! Parle doucement, s'il te plaît.
'Hush! Speak softly, please.' Andrea immediately hushes the boisterous actor. The interjection 'hush' is the standard French sound used to request silence.
Mon bébé dort dans la chambre.
'My baby is sleeping in the bedroom.' Andrea explains why they must remain extremely quiet. The verb 'sleeps' describes sleep in the present tense.
Oh pardon, je veux voir ta fille!
'Oh sorry, I want to see your daughter!' Jose expresses spontaneous affection for Andrea's infant. The feminine noun 'fille' means daughter or girl.
Non, reste ici dans le salon.
'No, stay here in the living room.' Andrea firmly directs him away from the nursery. The adverb 'here' points to the immediate location.
Tu es magnifique ce soir, Andréa!
'You are gorgeous tonight, Andrea!' Jose delivers a cheerful, drunken compliment to his agent. The temporal phrase 'this' refers to this evening or tonight.
Mais tu as bu beaucoup d'alcool!
'But you drank a lot of alcohol!' Andrea notices Jose's inebriated state right away. The quantifier 'beaucoup de' takes an invariable 'de' before the noun.
Oui, j'ai passé la soirée avec Laurence.
'Yes, I spent the evening with Laurence.' Jose reveals that he spent hours reminiscing with Laurence. The past participle 'spent' combines with 'have' to describe spending time.
Tu dois te reposer pour ton tournage.
'You must rest for your film shoot.' Andrea reminds him that a demanding camera crew awaits tomorrow. The modal verb 'must' indicates duty or obligation.
Je peux me servir à boire?
'Can I serve myself a drink?' Jose heads toward the kitchen counter looking for refreshments. The reflexive verb 'se servir' means to help oneself.
Bois seulement de l'eau fraîche maintenant.
'Drink only cold water now.' Andrea insists that alcohol is out of the question tonight. The restrictive adverb 'only' limits the choice to water.
D'accord, je vais me calmer un peu.

'All right, I am going to calm down a bit.' Jose relents and agrees to quiet down for the night. The near-future construction 'am going to' signals an immediate change in behavior. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.
Andréa! Ouvre la porte, c'est moi!
José? Qu'est-ce que tu fais là?
Quelle nuit incroyable, Andréa!
Chut! Parle doucement, s'il te plaît.
Mon bébé dort dans la chambre.
Oh pardon, je veux voir ta fille!
Non, reste ici dans le salon.
Tu es magnifique ce soir, Andréa!
Mais tu as bu beaucoup d'alcool!
Oui, j'ai passé la soirée avec Laurence.
Tu dois te reposer pour ton tournage.
Je peux me servir à boire?
Bois seulement de l'eau fraîche maintenant.
D'accord, je vais me calmer un peu.

Andrea manages to steer Jose Garcia into her living room without waking baby Flora. Exhausted by his antics and worried about his morning shoot, she prepares to keep a close eye on him. Now let's listen to the scene one last time.
Dors bien sur le canapé!
